mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month preceding the decision leads to a short-term discounting effect, lowering the present value of expected equity cash flows and thus producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the month prior to the decision
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in similar rising-rate regimes are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05), or the 5-day return is positive despite the rate spike.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2% in a month, it signals accelerating inflation expectations that compress real equity valuations, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Over a 5-year window, 60-day forward returns during similar inflation spikes are not significantly negative (p > 0.10), or the effect is explained by other variables.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS exceeding +10,000 for two consecutive months indicates strengthening labor market conditions, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In analogous labor-strong regimes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05), or the effect persists only during unemployment declines.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (billions of chained USD) grows by more than 5% in a quarter relative to the prior quarter, it reflects robust consumer and business demand, which elevates earnings growth forecasts and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly growth > +5% vs prior quarter
failure_condition: During comparable expansion quarters, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than average (p > 0.10), or the effect is absent after controlling for other demand proxies.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (monthly index) by more than 5% from the prior month signals supply-side weakness, lowering market confidence and depressing expected growth, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In similar contraction regimes, 5-day forward returns are not negative (p > 0.05), or the effect is mediated by other supply indicators.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in HOUST (units) and RSAFS (dollars) above their prior month averages by at least 3% each suggest coordinated strength in industrial production and retail activity, raising optimism for corporate earnings and supporting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In analogous periods with similar proxy moves, 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05), or the interaction effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 4.5% for three consecutive months indicates weaker wage pressures, which reduces inflationary risks and supports valuation expansion, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: During comparable low-unemployment/wage-pressure regimes, 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10), or the effect reverses during subsequent wage increases.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 3% for two consecutive months in a non-expansionary macro context, it suggests accommodative policy persistence, lowering real rates and boosting equity valuations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 3.0% for 2 consecutive months AND macro context is not expansionary
failure_condition: In similar non-expansionary settings, 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05), or the effect is absent after controlling for other liquidity proxies.
